{{Short description|Japanese physics professor (1934–2018)}}
{{nihongo|'''Gaku Konishi'''|小西 岳|Konishi Gaku|extra=}} (1934 in [[Minoh, Osaka]] – 17 January 2018<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.akademio-de-esperanto.org/akademio/index.php?title=Konstruata_tabelo_de_%C4%89iuj_membroj_de_AdE |title=Konstruata tabelo de ĉiuj membroj de AdE |website=[[Akademio de Esperanto]] |access-date=2018-02-21}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.facebook.com/Japana.Esperanto.Instituto/posts/1429910093785393 |title=日本エスペラント協会 Japana Esperanto-Instituto |date=25 January 2018 |website=www.facebook.com |access-date=2018-02-21}}</ref>) was a Japanese physics professor at [[Kwansei Gakuin University]] and an [[Esperanto|Esperantist]].

==Esperanto movement==
Konishi was a committed Esperantist who first began learning [[Esperanto]] in 1948, at the age of 13. Within the Esperanto movement he was active in the antinationalist [[Sennacieca Asocio Tutmonda|SAT]] association and in the [[Kansai region|Kansai League of Esperanto Groups]], the second-largest Japanese Esperanto federation. He was formerly a member of the [[Akademio de Esperanto|Academy of Esperanto]] and a [[Japana Esperanto-Instituto|Japanese Esperanto Institute]] councillor.

Konishi translated extensively from [[Japanese language|Japanese]] into Esperanto, including prose works like [[Yasunari Kawabata]]'s ''[[Snow Country]]'' (雪国, ''Yukiguni'', Esperanto title ''"La Neĝa Lando"'') and of [[Kenji Miyazawa]]'s ''[[Night on the Galactic Railroad]]'' (銀河鉄道の夜, ''Ginga Tetsudō no Yoru'', Esperanto title ''"Nokto de la galaksia fervojo"''), etc. He translated many songs, compiled songbooks and composed original songs, melodies and poetry. He also wrote original works in Esperanto.<ref name="ovpl">Josip Pleadin, ''[http://katalogo.uea.org/index.php?inf=7623 Ordeno de Verda Plumo]'' ("Order of the Green Plume", a biographical lexicon of Esperanto authors and translators), Grafokom, 2006: Đurđevac, 272 pp. {{ISBN|953-96975-5-7}}</ref> A collection of his [[science fiction]] works appeared in 1976 under the title ''Vage tra la dimensioj'' (次元の間をさまよって, "Rambling through the dimensions").

He also wrote textbooks, was chief editor of ''Nova Esperanto-Japana Vortaro'', an Esperanto-Japanese dictionary published by the Japanese Esperanto Institute,<ref name="siba">Zyun'iti Sibayama, {{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120529115258/http://groups.yahoo.com/group/landa-agado/message/839|title=Japanio: Premio Ossaka al Konisi Gaku}} ("Japan: Ossaka Award to Gaku Konishi"), 19 July 2000. Accessed 2011-02-09</ref> and was active in many other areas. He wrote in Japanese about [[Esperanto grammar]] and contributed to the propagation of the Esperanto movement by [[copy editing|copy-editing]] its book and magazine articles for correct grammar.

==Awards==
For his science fiction novel ''La kosmoŝipo Edeno n-ro 5'' ("Spaceship Eden No. 5") he was awarded an honourable mention in the prose category at the 1965 [[Belartaj Konkursoj]], the Esperanto movement's annual fine arts competition.<ref name="uk65">[http://esperanto.net/literaturo/bk/bk.html Belartaj Konkursoj de UEA]. Accessed 2011-02-09.</ref> In October 2000 the Japanese Esperanto Congress bestowed the ''Premio Ossaka'' on Konishi, in recognition of "his outstanding translations of Japanese ''belles-lettres'' and songs into Esperanto."<ref name="ovpl" /> Given in memory of [[Kenji Osaka]] (1888-1969), father of the Japanese Esperanto movement, the ''Premio Ossaka'' is the most prestigious adjudicated award for Esperantists in Japan.<ref name="siba" />

At the opening of the 2007 [[World Congress of Esperanto]] in [[Yokohama]] he was elected an honorary member of the [[Universal Esperanto Association|Universal Esperanto Association (UEA)]]

==Other works==

===Original Esperanto writings===
* ''Promenado en gramatiko.'' Esperanto grammar in Japanese medium. JELK, Osaka: 1986. 104 pages.  
* ''Pado de Gramatiko'', primer, anthology and grammar.
* Songbooks ''Venu amikoj'' ("Come, friends") and ''Kantoj karmemoraj'' ("Songs to remember loved ones").

===Translations into Esperanto===
* ''La ĝemelaj steloj'' ("Twin stars and other stories of Kenji Miyazawa")
* ''Notoj de la delto'' (デルタの記, "Notes from the delta"), reportage on the [[Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki|nuclear bombing]] of the city of [[Hiroshima]]
* ''La ĉevalo de Motizuki'' ("Motizuki's horse"), [[choir|choral suite]] from [[Katuiti Honda]]'s ''Vilaĝo en batalkampo'' (戦場の村, "Village in a battlefield"), reportage of the [[Vietnam War]]
* contributing translator and editor of the photojournalism book ''Hiroshima-[[Nagasaki]]'' about the two cities destroyed by nuclear bombs.
* ''La edzino de kuracisto Hanaoka Seisyû'' (English title, "The Doctor's Wife") by [[Sawako Ariyoshi]], Japana Esperanto-Instituto, Tokyo: 2008, 157pp. {{ISBN|978-4-88887-056-6}}

===Translation of Japanese literature===
* "Dancistino de Izu" (伊豆の踊り子, "[[The Dancing Girl of Izu|The Izu Dancer]]"), by [[Yasunari Kawabata]]
* ''El Japana Literaturo'' (日本文学選集, "Anthology of Japanese Literature")
* "La Tombo de Lampiroj" (火垂るの墓, ''[[Grave of the Fireflies (novel)|Grave of the Fireflies]]'') by [[Akiyuki Nosaka]] 
* ''Postmilita Japana Antologio'' (戦後日本文学選集, "Postwar Japanese Anthology")<ref name="works">{{Cite web |url=http://www.bongo.ne.jp/~teg/membro/konisi.htm |title=Gaku Konishi works |access-date=2011-02-10 |archive-date=2011-07-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720014744/http://www.bongo.ne.jp/~teg/membro/konisi.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref>
